newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIA GOVT BUYS TWO-THIRDS OF FARMERS' WHEAT.
newsitem.headline: CROATIA GOVT BUYS TWO-THIRDS OF FARMERS' WHEAT.

text.p: The Croatian government bought two-thirds of the domestic wheat harvest, enough to satisfy the country's domestic needs, Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic told a news conference on Thursday.
The former Yugoslav republic harvested 884,000 tonnes of wheat this year and is planning to increase the amount of land under wheat by 36 percent in the autumn, he said.
The amount of land sown in rape seed and rye will be doubled to 10,000 and 3,000 hectares respectively.
The government bought more than 600,000 tonnes of wheat from farmers this year. "All the harvested wheat planned to be bought was bought from producers," Dominikovic said.
The export of surplus wheat, however, is banned until the end of September.
Dominikovic said the ministry supported the harvest with loans worth 214.5 million kuna.

It is planning to increase the amount of agricultural land under wheat to 280,000 hectares in the autumn, which should yield around 1.1 million tonnes, still short of the pre-war 1.5-million-tonne level, Dominikovic said.
He said the price of meat should fall between five and 13 percent this month, following the government decision last month to raise import duties on 48 agricultural products.
The new protection prices "have generated a good response from farmers", he said. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
